q: Borel equivalence relations (countable Borel equivalence relations, CBER) are equivalence relations on Polish spaces with Borel graphs. The simplest non-trivial is E₀ (tail equivalence on {0,1}^ℕ). Dye's theorem states:
opts: All CBERs are smooth (Borel reducible to equality)
E₀ is the unique minimal non-smooth CBER — every non-smooth CBER contains E₀
CBERs have only finitely many classes
All CBERs have the same Borel complexity
exp: Dye's theorem (in descriptive set theory formulation): E₀ is Borel reducible to every non-smooth CBER. E₀ is not smooth (no Borel assignment of canonical elements to classes), but it is the minimum non-smooth CBER. This begins the rich theory of Borel equivalence relations.
